title: Muhammad Ali: Float Like Greatness
description: From Olympic gold to global icon—five chapters of the Greatest.

questions.question: Which boxer promised to 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'?
questions.explanation: Ali's cornerman Drew Bundini Brown came up with the line; Ali made it immortal.

questions.question: Young Muhammad Ali won Olympic gold as Cassius Clay at which 1960 Games?
After his 1960 Rome gold, where did Ali say he tossed his Olympic medal?
Ali later wrote that he threw his medal in the Ohio River—what injustice did he say drove him to it?
questions.explanation: The story comes from his 1975 autobiography. Friends such as photographer Howard Bingham said he simply lost the medal—but the anger at being refused service in his hometown was real.

questions.question: Recognizing the racial discrimination he protested, officials gave Ali a replacement medal in what year?

imageHint: Boxing gloves raised high in victory, symbolizing triumph and championship
